captions.detailed: A 3D printable sign or nameplate featuring the embossed text 'HELLO WORLD'. The plate has a rounded, rectangular base with integrated support feet on the bottom edge for standing upright. It features detailed geometric elements simulating a 3D printer nozzle and guide rod positioned over the text, giving it a stylized, 'in-progress' printing appearance.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric 'Hello World' nameplate in OpenSCAD that simulates a 3D printer in action. The user should be able to customize the text string, plate thickness, horizontal spacing, and select different base styles (like solid or feet) as well as toggle a hanging hole.
captions.factory: The script uses a custom 'text' module that extracts character polygons from a 2D font library and extrudes them using linear_extrude. The main body is built by unioning a rounded plate (created using minkowski on a cube and cylinder), a simulated guide rod, an extruder carriage, and a nozzle consisting of cylinders. The entire assembly is constructed using conditional 'if' statements to handle base styles, hanging holes, and output styles, combined with difference operations to cut out the nozzle paths.
